evidence_quotes.agenda: (not asked -- rep asked 'is this a good time for you?' then went straight into item-list questions, no biggest-concerns question ever asked)
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: "I'm looking for a moving partial items from my house because because of how family issue" ... later: "right now, I'm in trouble for money...I need to see how much you're going to [cost] since it's a separation" -- both times the rep answered with 'Got it' / 'No problem' and pivoted straight back to logistics/price with zero follow-up on either disclosure.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: we just prorate every fifteen minutes...you only pay after the move is completed with the actual time use for the move.

top_strength: Gave a clear, well-personalized time/cost range for a mixed-inventory partial move and made an explicit close attempt ('Would you like to get this moved scheduled?').
coaching_note: The customer disclosed real financial stress tied to a separation twice and it was never acknowledged or explored -- this is exactly the 'asked nothing of it' failure mode the rubric is built to catch; slow down and dig into a concern like this instead of pivoting straight back to logistics.
